correctness.rationale: For n>=2k and fixed k, the necessary order-pattern equality between v[1..n-k] and v[k+1..n] defines an increasing bijection f from the ranks outside the last k entries onto the ranks outside the first k entries. Specifying the ordered first-k tuple and unordered final-k set uniquely determines f; iterating f along all k residue classes reconstructs at most one valid permutation, with domain-end and duplicate checks. All (n+1)^k final-rank insertion sequences yield unique edge-labeled walks (including parallel edges), giving O_k(n^(3k+1)) arithmetic operations. For k=3 and n>3 only the two monotone loop triples are nonsimple rooted closed walks, hence C3=(W3-2)/3. Independent full-graph weighted 3-walk trace reconstructions for n=3..7 matched counts 26,40,56,56,76 and the corresponding package census (n>=6). Source C++ and Python finite algorithms and exact 19-row table were read; full 19-row C++ run was not independently executed. This is a structural all-n fixed-k algorithm proof plus bounded diagnostics, NOT a general closed count formula.

value.rationale: Question 24 on cycles in the natural permutation-overlap multigraph motivates the finite exact invariant. Unique boundary-rank reconstruction replaces factorially many vertices by O_k(n^(2k)) candidate descriptions and gives exact labeled walk counts in polynomial time for each fixed length; the nineteen-point three-cycle census is an independently useful nontrivial finite calculation rather than a known-table recomputation. The finite table does not claim all-n enumeration.

limitations: The complexity exponent depends on fixed k and requires n>=2k, not an FPT algorithm or uniform polynomial in both inputs.
